description: Redevelopment of the site to provide a building comprising a self-storage facility (Class B8) and flexible office/light industrial use (Class E(g)(i)/E(g)(iii)), together with associated car and cycle parking, refuse storage, access and landscaping.
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [16587-DMWR-A-PL-0006 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0007 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0004 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0005 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0003 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0008 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0002 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0301 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0302 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0303 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0101 Rev A, 6587-DMWR-A-PL-0103 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0104 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0105 Rev A, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0200 Rev A: Received 26/01/2024. 9379 - ES - ZZ - L10-DR - C � 601 Rev T2: Received 26/04/2024. 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0300 Rev B, 6587-DMWR-A-PL-0100 Rev B, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0201 Rev B, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0202 Rev B, 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0010 Rev B: Received 01/05/2024. 16587-DMWR-A-PL-0001 Rev B: Received 15/05/2024. P23-0372_EN_0001_F_0001, P23-0372_EN_0002_C_0001: Received 28/05/2024. 9379 - ES - ZZ - XX - DR - C � 600 Rev T3: Received 21/06/2024].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - No development above ground level shall take place until full details (including product specifications) and samples of all materials to be used in the construction of all of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details must include a detailed schedule of materials, a photographic sample board and rendered drawings, elevations and sections at a sufficient scale (1:20 or 1:50) to illustrate how all external materials will appear together.
The physical samples and details shall include: 

(a)	Brick/stonework (including brick, stone, masonry, brick panels, feature brick panel, brick framing feature and mortar on-site sample panel, minimum one metre by one metre) including all mortar colours, joint type, brick bond;
(b)	Cladding materials / render (including specifications where relevant);
(c)	Tiles / roof covering; including parapet coping / capping materials, dormers and canopies;
(d)	Window types; and sectional drawings of reveals / sills / head details 
(e)	Balustrading treatment to balconies and roof areas (including details / sections / materials); and handrails
(f)	Any other materials/details / fittings to be used (including solar panels, extract vents, rainwater goods, boiler flues etc.), with sections and on-site samples where appropriate
(g)	Any other materials / details / fittings to be used (including solar panels, extract vents, boiler flues etc.), with sections and on-site samples where appropriate. 
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the area.

Condition : 5 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein. 
Reason: In the interests of Air Quality and to satisfy the requirements of policy EQ4 of the adopted Local Plan.

Condition : 6 - Automatic real-time air quality monitoring shall take place during demolition and construction as required by the Mayor of London SPD. Prior to the commencement of development, a monitoring plan shall be developed and submitted, for approval in writing, by the Local Planning Authority. The monitoring shall continuously monitor concentrations of PM10 and PM2.5 utilising the traffic light system for recording dust alerts in accordance with the Institute of Air Quality Management Guidance on Air Quality Monitoring in the Vicinity of Demolition and Construction Sites, 2018. Any exceedances of the red criteria shall be immediately raised with the site manager to investigate the cause of the exceedance. When a red exceedance is recorded, site operations shall be ceased until mitigation measures have been put in place. It shall be specified that a 3-month baseline monitoring period will be undertaken prior to any construction in accordance with the IAQM Guidance on the assessment of dust from demolition and construction 2024. Additionally, a record of any complaints from residents shall be kept and measures taken to address complaints.
Reason: To ensure the protection of public health from the impacts of dust emissions during the demolition and construction phases.

Condition : 7 - Prior to first use of the development, the applicant shall have entered into a binding arrangement with the Council to make an agreed contribution to the Council's Carbon Offset Fund, in accordance with the zero carbon strategy set out in the Energy Statement hereby approved to an amount that equates to the shortfall in required energy savings to meet the 'zero carbon' target.
 Reason: In order to ensure the development meets sustainability standards.

Condition : 8 - Noise from fixed plant shall not exceed levels greater than 10 dB below background (LA90) noise levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby dwellings. Noise levels shall be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance.
Reason: In order to ensure that existing residents do not suffer an unreasonable level of noise and disturbance from plant equipment.

Condition : 9 - Based upon guidance contained within BS 5228:2009 + A1:2014: Noise, noise levels from construction works at nearby existing and proposed residential receptors shall not exceed the following construction noise criteria:
-Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst-affected residential property during the following time periods:
-Monday to Friday (08:00 � 18:00 hours) 	 
-Saturday (08:00 to 13:00 hours)
Works outside of the standard hours will be subject to prior agreement and prior notice will be provided to the London Borough of Hounslow.
Reason: In order to ensure that existing residents do not suffer an unreasonable level of noise and disturbance during the construction phase.

Condition : 10 - Prior to first occupation of the development, an updated Delivery and Servicing Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current 41 guidance such as that issued by Transport for London and shall include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements, physical as well as managerial, for the servicing, including emergency vehicle access, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation.  The Plan shall be carried out as approved. The approved measures shall be implemented before the first use of the development hereby permitted and shall be so maintained for the life of the development.  
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives in accordance with adopted.

Condition : 11 - Prior to the first use of the development, a Car Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include details of how the car parking spaces will be managed, measures to ensure that the delivery and servicing area is kept free for its intended purpose, and include details of both active and passive EV charging provisions as required by the London Plan. The site shall thereafter operate in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied as to the details of the development and to ensure that parking spaces are available in accordance with Policy T6 of the London Plan and Local Plan Policy EC2.

Condition : 13 - Prior to the first use of the development, full details (including manufacturers' specifications) of secure covered cycle parking facilities that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance for the employees of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The short stay cycle parking facilities for visitors shall also include details of cargo bike facilities. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the development is first brought into use. The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 14 - Before the development hereby permitted is first brought into use, a finalised Travel Plan, in accordance with current Council and TfL guidance, comprising immediate, continuing and long-term measures to promote and encourage a reduction in car use shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved Travel Plan shall be implemented upon occupation, and thereafter monitored and reviewed in accordance with the agreed Travel Plan targets and timescales to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives, including a reduction in single occupancy car journeys and the increased use of public transport, walking and cycling.

Condition : 15 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant shall submit a final detailed drainage design, including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form], to the Local Planning Authority, for approval in writing, that will be aligned with the Drainage Strategy (Revision T5 - 24/05/2024) and associated drawings. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components shall also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI13, the Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, and the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 16 - No building hereby permitted shall be brought into use until evidence (including photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to the Local Planning Authority, for approval in writing, to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the approved details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI13, the Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, and the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 17 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work.
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local planning authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where it is deemed necessary to secure adequate safety for future site users. 
(iv)	Suitable testing shall be undertaken in accordance with the potential contaminants identified in the Conceptual Site

Condition : 18 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 19 - During the development:
The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. 
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 20 - Prior to the development is first brought into use:
The agreed scheme for remediation, if required, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 21 - If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the Local Planning Authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice. 
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. 
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.

Condition : 22 - Prior to first use of the development, details (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the following sustainable sourcing of materials requirements:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- 	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
-      No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials in accordance with the London Plan Policy SI2 and the Mayor of London's Sustainable Design and Construction SPG.

Condition : 23 - a.)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the hereby approved Energy and Sustainability Statement Version 1 Rev D received on 08/05/2024. 
b.)	Prior to first use of the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions, and achieved a 98.01% reduction in emissions.
c.)	Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, suitable devices for the monitoring of the low and zero carbon technologies shall have been installed, and the monitored data shall be submitted automatically to a monitoring web-platform at daily intervals for a period of three years from the point of full operation. The data shall be made available to the local planning authority on request for a period of five years.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions in accordance with London Plan Policy SI2 and the London Borough of Hounslow Local Plan Policy EQ1.

Condition : 24 - (a) No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a BREEAM preliminary-assessment estimator (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating how an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating will be achieved.
(b) Within eight months of work starting on site, a BREEAM Design Stage certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating will be achieved.
(c) A BREEAM Post-Construction Review certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating has been achieved. 
Reason: In order to ensure the highest standard of sustainable design and construction.
Supporting notes: Details submitted should state if BREEAM will be fully fitted, shell and core or shell only. Additional BREEAM Refurbishment and Fit-Out details will likely be required where not specified as fully fitted.

Condition : 26 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include;
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat,
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development,
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 27 - Prior to the commencement of the development, details of a scheme for the removal and management of invasive species (False acacia and buddleja) observed onsite shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Works shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed details. 
Reason: To ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat and secure opportunities for the enhancement of nature conservation in accordance with the NPPF and Local Plan Policy GB7.

Condition : 28 - Prior to the first use of the development, the applicant shall have entered into a s278 agreement with Transport for London for the works to the Transport for London highway. The works shall be completed as agreed with Transport for London prior to first use of the development. 
Reason: In the interests of highway safety.
